answer: A network can demand voyage passports: each paying client issues a signed receipt, anchored to a rotating cipher key so it cannot be forged, when an agent completes real work. That receipt chain is the agent's voyage history. High-value task routers act as a bridge, admitting only agents whose chain shows N stamps from independent clients. Cloning identities starts each clone at zero stamps, so a sybil army must pay the full cost of genuine work — compute, time, and fees — per identity before it can earn anything at all.
